parsed_output.analysis: The PlantUML model captures most of the top-level flow and the three InMotion substates with their entry and transition labels, but it adds an unspecified self-loop in DoorsClosing, it leaves Approaching without an exit path to stopping, and it models the EmergencyStopping outputs as a continuous do activity and re-uses the name Obstacle Detected for both the incoming trigger and the outgoing signal. The parent-level InMotion → Stopping transition also bypasses the Approaching substate where arrival would be expected.

issues.reason: The specification describes DoorsClosing only as the initial state that transitions to InMotion on Closed/SendDeparted. The model adds an internal [*] --> DoorsClosing self transition with no trigger/action, which is not described in the specification.

issues.issue: Approaching substate has no defined exit
issues.reason: Specification 10 says the system remains in Approaching while nearing destination until it is ready to stop or decelerate, and specification 2 says InMotion can go to Stopping on Arrived/Stop, Send Arrived. The model provides no transition out of Approaching, so there is no modeled path from Approaching to Stopping/arriving, and the parent-level InMotion --> Stopping transition bypasses the substate hierarchy.

issues.issue: Stopping transition is modeled at parent InMotion level instead of from Approaching
issues.reason: Arrival logically occurs in the Approaching phase. The specification describes InMotion substates and that the system remains in Approaching until ready to stop. Modeling the Arrived transition directly from the parent InMotion decouples arrival from the Approaching substate.

issues.issue: EmergencyStopping output modeled as continuous do activity and trigger name collides with output
issues.reason: Specification 3 says EmergencyStopping includes the actions Emergency Stop and sends the Obstacle Detected signal on entry to the state. The model uses Obstacle Detected as the transition trigger into EmergencyStopping and then models Send Obstacle Detected as a do activity, implying continuous sending, and reuses the same name for event and signal.
issues.where: InMotion --> EmergencyStopping : Obstacle Detected and state EmergencyStopping { EmergencyStopping: do/Send Obstacle Detected }

issues.issue: Emergency Stop action modeled as entry only, sending of Obstacle Detected modeled as do instead of entry
issues.reason: Specification 3 describes EmergencyStopping as including both Emergency Stop and sending Obstacle Detected as part of entering the state. The model makes Emergency Stop an entry action but makes Send Obstacle Detected a do activity, which changes the timing semantics from a one-time entry notification to continuous emission.
issues.where: state EmergencyStopping { EmergencyStopping: entry/Emergency Stop; EmergencyStopping: do/Send Obstacle Detected }

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
